clue.text: Pretty dated, like comedians Benny and Harry?

blocks.note: first meaning: very old, an everyday idiom for ancient
second, playful meaning: Benny Hill and Harry Hill are both comedians surnamed Hill, so their age is that of the Hills

explanation.walkthrough: Benny Hill and Harry Hill are British TV comedians; the question mark flags the joke of reading the idiom as the age of those two Hills.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes anything extremely old, so it fits something that is quite out of date.

clue.text: Staggered like hedonist getting drunk

indicators.note: someone drunk lurches about, so these letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: as is a synonym of like in comparisons
the letters of this word are the fodder

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker stumbles about, reeling after too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggered' reads as a drunk's gait, matching the surface, but here it means amazed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be staggered is to be greatly surprised, the same shock as being amazed.

clue.text: Hunter – one that's charged after soldiers

indicators.note: after places the first part of the wordplay behind the second in the finished word

blocks.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: A hunter accused of an offence following a raid by troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is the great hunter of Greek myth, now a constellation.

clue.text: The lady demolished extra pasty

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked down and its parts lie scattered in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A woman wolfs down a second Cornish pasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' looks like the baked pie being eaten, but it is the adjective meaning pale-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: Deathly pale means extremely white-faced, like a corpse, so very pasty in complexion.

clue.text: Initially sharp nail filed down here?

definitions.text: Initially sharp nail filed down here?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows it
filing wears down the tip, so the start of the word is taken off and replaced

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
a talon is a claw, an animal's nail

explanation.surface: A beautician files a client's pointed nail smooth.
explanation.walkthrough: TALON loses its T, which is filed off, and S from sharp takes its place, giving SALON; the whole clue also describes a nail salon.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty or nail salon is the shop where manicurists file customers' nails.

clue.text: Those most in need of bread depended on priests, essentially

definitions.text: Those most in need of bread
definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; this phrase reads as a noun

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so its middle letters are kept

blocks.note: hung on means depended on
the middle of this word, losing its outer letters

explanation.surface: The poor who needed food relied on the clergy's charity.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is the adjective meaning most hungry, used of those people.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in need of bread means wanting food, so the most hungry are the most needy.

clue.text: Hidden source of MDMA located in raid

indicators.note: located in means set inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a hold-up is an armed robbery or raid
E is slang for ecstasy, the drug made from MDMA

explanation.surface: Police raid a lab where an ecstasy supply is concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: MDMA is the chemical name of ecstasy, known on the street simply as E.
explanation.definitionFit: To be holed up is to be hiding out, staying concealed somewhere.

clue.text: Stirring novels set in romantic locations

indicators.note: stirring mixes things round, so these letters are mixed into another order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Exciting romance fiction takes place in idyllic settings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' reads as an adjective for thrilling novels, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A love nest is a private hideaway for lovers, a romantic retreat.

clue.text: Set of players communicated frustration to audience

indicators.note: addressed to an audience means heard rather than read, so the sound matters

blocks.note: a sigh expresses frustration

explanation.surface: An actor huffs in exasperation at the theatre crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' and 'audience' suggest a theatre, but the players form a sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team, the group of players fielded in a match.

clue.text: Tesla with smart technology starts to go astray in forest

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters

blocks.note: T is the symbol for the tesla, a unit of magnetic flux density
artificial intelligence
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A self-driving Tesla with clever software wanders off course among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car maker, but it is the scientific unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The taiga is the vast coniferous forest belt of Siberia and northern Canada.

clue.text: Hardy pine rebuffed infernal thing

indicators.note: to rebuff is to push back, so the word is turned back to front

blocks.note: to pine for something is to long for it
a devil is a creature of hell

explanation.surface: A tough conifer drives off a demon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' and 'pine' together suggest a robust tree, but pine is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy means robust and enduring, and the robust tend to survive to old age.

clue.text: Stimulating discontented nation, ad in Indy ushered in next age of Methuselah

indicators.note: stimulating stirs things up, so all these letters are stirred into a new order
losing its contents leaves a word with only its outside letters

blocks.note: the outside letters of this word

blocks.clueFragment: ad in Indy ushered in next
blocks.note: these words are taken whole as fodder

explanation.surface: A rousing advert in the Independent heralds the setter Methuselah's next birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is called Methuselah, and this is puzzle number 11,969, so the clue celebrates the number. The Indy is the Independent newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis records that the patriarch Methuselah lived for 969 years, the longest lifespan in the Bible.

clue.text: Bewitching bands use pipes

blocks.note: a posse is a band of people
to pipe is to sing in a high voice

explanation.surface: Musical groups play bagpipes that cast a spell on listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bewitching' reads as charming, but it means taking control by spirit or spell, as in demonic possession.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit possessing someone takes control of them, as a witch's spell or enchantment does.

clue.text: See 11
Axes cut perfect wooden instrument

blocks.note: the x and y axes of a graph
to lop is to cut off
to hone is to refine or perfect

explanation.surface: Woodcutters' axes shape a flawless musical instrument from timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' suggests choppers for wood, but it means the axes of a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: A xylophone is a percussion instrument of tuned wooden bars struck with mallets.

clue.text: Stars and stripes possibly involved GIs in a sin

indicators.note: something involved is tangled up, so these letters are tangled into another order

blocks.note: the letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: The American flag shown in a scandal implicating US soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars and stripes' looks like the US flag, but here it is military badges of rank, stars and chevrons.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are badges of rank or office, such as an officer's stars or a sergeant's stripes.

clue.text: Goats and sheep regularly knocked back green stuff for dinner

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
knocked back means sent backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
the first, third and fifth letters, continuing the every-other pattern

explanation.surface: Livestock gulped down the grass meant for their evening feed.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternation runs across both animal words as one string, ignoring the joining word between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is a green Italian sauce of basil and pine nuts served with pasta.

clue.text: English court adopting the French style

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one piece is taken inside the other

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
CT is the abbreviation for court
la is the French feminine definite article

explanation.surface: An English court takes on French fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliance or flair in performance, a showy panache.

clue.text: Coordinated kit ultimately spoilt tennis player's aim?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: the closing letter of this word
a tennis player aims to win a set

explanation.surface: A tennis star's matching outfit ruined their game plan.
explanation.walkthrough: A twinset is a matching cardigan and jumper, a classic British women's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinset is a matching jumper and cardigan worn together, a coordinated outfit.

clue.text: Mocks held by those controlling pupils

blocks.note: a court or council sat, that is, a session was held
the iris controls the size of the eye's pupil

explanation.surface: Mock exams run by the teachers in charge of schoolchildren.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mocks' and 'pupils' suggest school practice exams; the pupils are in the eye, and Mocks is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To satirise someone is to ridicule them through humour, which is mocking.

clue.text: Paper from shop with some hit piece rolled up

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the letters lie inside the words given
in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, the opposite way

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning these three words

explanation.surface: A newspaper attack article bought at a shop gets rolled up.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is the slip of paper a shop gives as proof of purchase.

clue.text: Youngsters getting kind of onion with layers

blocks.note: spring onion is a variety of onion
hens are layers of eggs

explanation.surface: Kids are served an onion with lots of skins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layers' reads as an onion's rings, but here it means egg-laying birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring chicken is a young person; the idiom usually appears as no spring chicken.

clue.text: "Hotel all right?" "I don't know what to tell you – it's rubbish"

blocks.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
OK means all right

blocks.clueFragment: I don't know what to tell you
blocks.note: um is the hesitant noise of someone lost for words

explanation.surface: A guest asks if the hotel is fine and the reluctant reply is that it is awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Hokum is nonsense or claptrap, talk that is worthless.

clue.text: Half the periodic table needed by one fragrant substance

blocks.note: the periodic table lists the elements; half of that word
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A chemist needs half the elements to make one perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: The periodic table is the table of the elements, and half of that word is its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin from tropical trees used in varnishes, incense and perfume.

clue.text: Maybe Miss Jean Brodie snuck out, forgetting all about primes

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving out, here every letter standing at a prime-numbered position

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A schoolmistress sneaked away, ignoring her best girls.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters 2, 3, 5 and 7 go, leaving the first, fourth, sixth and eighth. Miss Jean Brodie is the Edinburgh teacher of Muriel Spark's novel, whose favourites were the crème de la crème, close to 'primes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Jean Brodie is an Edinburgh schoolteacher, an example of someone Scottish.

clue.text: One half of couple picking up food from Chinese restaurant

definitions.text: One half of couple picking up food from Chinese restaurant

blocks.note: surface: one partner of a pair collecting a takeaway

blocks.clueFragment: picking up food from Chinese restaurant
blocks.note: setter's reading: one of the pair of utensils used to lift food in Chinese dining

explanation.walkthrough: The couple seems to be two people fetching a takeaway; it is a pair of eating utensils, and picking up is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopsticks come in pairs and are used to lift food to the mouth in Chinese cuisine.

clue.text: Cryptic enigmatically features ancient folk

indicators.note: the words feature the answer, holding it inside their letters

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A puzzling clue mysteriously mentions a long-gone people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe of East Anglia, led by Boudicca.

clue.text: My hot new setting puzzled person of a certain age

indicators.note: something puzzled is confused, so these letters are muddled into another order

blocks.note: the letters of these four words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A young adult is baffled by a trendy new place.
explanation.definitionFit: A twentysomething is someone aged between twenty and twenty-nine, a particular age bracket.
